text: I've created `filter.py`. It takes the HTML file path as its argument and removes JavaScript from the file in place. I tested it on a sample clean page (headers, tables, comments, styles, forms, entities, a data-image) and the output was byte-for-byte identical to the input. I also ran it against about 30 common XSS payloads, and every one came out with the script part removed or made inert. I only checked the output text; I didn't load the results in a browser to confirm nothing runs. **How it works:** it splits each tag into its name and attributes using the same rules browsers follow. Anything not judged dangerous is copied through exactly as it was. The file is read and written as raw bytes, so UTF-8 text such as `café` survives, and an unchanged file is never rewritten. It repeats the pass until nothing more changes, which catches tricks where removing one piece creates a new one, such as `<script>…`. **What it removes:** - **Whole elements, contents included:** `` and ``.
